full_judgment:
Civil Revision No. 3020 of 1992 and No. 3021 of 1992 are directed against the order dated 11.10.92 of the Senior Assistant Judge, Pathorghata, Barguna, in Miscellaneous Case No. 20 of 1991 and Miscellaneous Case 21 of 1991 filed under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-emption of land. Both the revisions are heard together and are disposed of by this judgment. 

 3. Mr. Md. Afzal Hussain challenges the propriety of the order of refusal to allow improvement cost contending that the order is contrary to the provisions of section 96(7)(b) of the Act. He also .submits that the learned Assistant Judge failed to indicate the provision of law which disentitles the petitioner to cost for improvement of the land made within 4 months. He cites the decision in the case of KM Raisuddin Vs. Taibuddin Mondal and others, BCR 1985 (AD) 430. The decision is not exactly on the point mooted at the bar. Section 96 (7)(b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 provides for payment of cost incurred for improvement of the land. But it does not indicate whether such expenses, if incurred within four months of the registration is to be allowed or not. In order to resolve this question, in my opinion, section 96(3)(b) is relevant which provides that the court on receipt of the application for pre-emution shall give notice to the transferee to appear and shall require to state, amongst others, what expenses he has incurred for improvement of the land transferred and to direct the applicant to deposit a further sum, if necessary, after holding an inquiry as to actual amount so spent. Clause(b) of sub-section (3) of section 96 of the Act enjoins upon the learned Assistant Judge duty to direct holding of an inquiry and to determine the actual amount of expenditure for development of the land. The impugned order rejecting application praying for improvement expenses for the land sought to be pre-empted is contrary to the provision of section 96(3)(b) read with sub-section 7(b) of the Act. Accordingly, I set aside the order impugned. I direct the learned Assistant Judge to accept the pleader commissioner's report in so far as it relates to the cost of improvement as indicated in the report along with the objection filed to that report and to determine the actual amount of the expenses for such improvement of the land.
